name: Idaho

context: ID 329: Residue standard keeps at least 2000 pounds per acre or 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
ID 340: Cover crops reduce wind and water erosion; time them so the soil is protected in the critical erosion period.
ID 380: A windbreak protects 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side, where H is the design height of the tallest row.
cover_rules: ID 340: Do not burn cover crop residue; set termination method and timing to meet the grower objective.
ID 340: In areas of limited soil moisture, end cover crop growth early enough to conserve soil moisture.
ID 340: Do not harvest cover crops for seed.
residue: ID 329: Keep at least 2000 pounds per acre or 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
ID 329: Stubble at least 10 inches for rows under 15 inches apart, at least 15 inches for rows of 15 inches or more, on 60% of the field.
ID 345: Keep at least 60 percent surface residue all year; do fall tillage as nearly perpendicular to prevailing winds as possible.
barriers: ID 589: Trap strips at least 15 feet wide if stubble is one foot or more tall, at least 25 feet wide if under one foot.
ID 603: Herbaceous barriers stand at least 1.5 feet tall, rows no more than 36 inches apart, spacing no more than 10 times barrier height.
ID 588: Cross wind ridges perpendicular to erosive wind, spaced no more than four times the designed ridge height.
windbreak: ID 380: Orient the windbreak perpendicular to the damaging wind; protected zone is 10H leeward and 2H windward.
ID 380: Set windbreak interval with erosion prediction so it stays within soil loss tolerance (T); choose species taller than the crop.
roughening: ID 609: For soils with wind erodibility I value of 104 or less, roughness must give a 25% reduction in potential erosion.
ID 609: Emergency tillage: wide chisel spacing or skip chiseling; start at the windward edge, ridges perpendicular to damaging wind.
ID 588: On sandy soils make cross wind ridges when soil is moist; ridges are temporary and work best with other practices.
grazing: ID 528: Plan grazing to leave adequate canopy, litter and trampled residue to protect the soil from wind.
ID 528: Minimize grazing impact on areas with high soil erosion potential.
ID 314: Choose the brush control method with the least soil disturbance if erosion potential is high and revegetation slow.
drought: ID 528: Write a contingency plan for episodic disturbances such as drought; follow it when conditions are not suitable for grazing.
ID 528: Use drought forecasting tools such as VegDRI to improve forage production projections.
seeding: ID 342: On light to medium textured soils dormant fall planting is preferred; on crusting heavy soils consider early spring.
ID 342: Critical area drill rates are 150 to 200 percent of normal; broadcast rates are 200 to 300 percent of normal drill rates.
ID 550: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis.
dont_seed: ID 340 note: Cereal rye can be very invasive and is generally not recommended in the Aberdeen PMC service area.
ID 342: Avoid seeding on irrigated land during very hot periods, mid to late June through mid-August.
ID 380: Do not use species on Federal or State invasive species or noxious weed lists in windbreaks.
pasture: ID 512: Select plants that give maximum ground cover to protect the soil from wind and water erosion.
ID 512: Where animals congregate, consider persistent species that tolerate close grazing and trampling.
ID 550: Species selected must give adequate cover to control erosion by wind and water within an acceptable period.
crp: ID 327: Conservation cover must maintain plant biomass and cover to hold erosion within tolerable soil loss.
disturbed: ID 342: Mulch plantings as necessary to establish them and other disturbed areas as needed to prevent erosion.
ID 342: Species, seeding rates, seedbed preparation and method must be specified before critical area seeding.
dunes: ID 342: Dune plants must survive burial by blowing sand and sand blasting; include sand fences or brush matting.
ID 550 note: Mammoth wildrye stops soil movement on well-drained inland sand dunes; full stand seeding rate 15 lb/ac.
ID 550 note: Fourwing saltbush is well suited to sand dunes and deep sandy soil.

cover.name: Barley
cover.note: Full seeding rate; seeding depth 1.0-2.0 inches.

cover.name: Oat
cover.note: Full rate; seeding depth 0.75-1.5 inch. Does not fare well in hot, dry weather.

cover.name: Cereal rye
cover.note: Full rate; generally not recommended in the Aberdeen PMC service area.

cover.name: Hairy vetch
cover.note: Full stand rate; 6.5 lbs/ac in the 8 way cool season mix.

cover.name: Radish
cover.note: Full stand rate; 1 lbs/ac in the 8 way mix.

coverPlant.text: ID 340 note: Winter wheat cover is planted in late August to mid-September; plant no later than October 1st in southern Idaho for wind erosion cover.
ID 340 note: Fall-seeded triticale goes in late August to mid-September for adequate growth before winter.
ID 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and terminate as late as practical to maximize biomass.

seedWin.text: ID 342: MLRA 9 and 11: spring before 4/15, fall (irrigated only) before 9/20, dormant after 11/1.
ID 342: MLRA 10, 13, 25: spring before 5/15, fall (irrigated only) before 9/10, dormant after 10/20.
ID 342: MLRA 43A, 43B, 43C: spring before 5/15, fall (irrigated only) before 9/1, dormant after 10/20.

mixes.title: Loamy 10-13 inch example mix (drill, applied lb/ac)
mixes.note: Example from PMTN 24 for a LOAMY 10-13 ARTRW8/PSSPS site; rates are applied drill rates.

shrubs.name: Winterfat
advice: ID 550 note: Winterfat is long-lived native sub-shrub on dry saline to alkaline soils with 7 to16 inches annual precipitation.
ID 550 note: Winterfat full seeding mix rate is 5 lb/ac (10 percent of the example mix).

shrubs.name: Fourwing saltbush
advice: ID 550 note: Fourwing saltbush suits deep, well-drained sandy soil and sand dunes; very tolerant of saline soils.
ID 550 note: It is mainly found in 8 to 14 inch annual precipitation zones.

shrubs.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
advice: ID 550 note: Rubber rabbitbrush grows in loamy, sandy, gravelly to clay-alkaline soils.
ID 550 note: It vigorously invades disturbed sites such as burned areas, roadcuts and overgrazed rangelands.

shrubs.name: Big sagebrush
advice: ID 550 note: Big sagebrush grows 1 to 15 feet tall in 8 to 18 inch annual precipitation zones.
ID 550 note: Wyoming big sagebrush is 10 percent of the example loamy mix, 0.025 lb/ac applied.
